stance.label: Short-term bearish, selling is fading and buyers have not arrived; long-term in the bottom zone

headline: The prior low held again as sellers thin out: realized losses ran under half of last week's peak. Buyers are still absent and $58,525 is not safe.
summary: Short-term bearish, with selling fading: with US markets back, a push to $62,139 was sold, realized losses on the retest of the prior low were under half of Nov 20, and options protection did not get cheaper. Long-term bullish: total unrealized profit is down to 33.2% of market cap and MVRV Z sits in the lowest 7% of four years, both bottom-zone readings. A close below $58,525 loses the prior low; ETF inflows and a close back above $64,000 would mean buyers are back.

watch.label: 200-day MA
watch.note: 16 straight closes below; the close needs +20.0% to get back above

overview.lead: The first day US markets were back tested both ends of the range: the push up turned at the supply waiting to get out even, the dip was caught about $200 above the prior low, and the close sat in the lower third of the day's range.
points: Close $59,864, high $62,139, low $58,729; volume was 1.85x the prior day and 1.11x the 20-day average (Kraken).
US stocks rallied in a half session, S&P 500 +1.6% and Nasdaq +2.3% (AP); BTC did not follow and was sold from its high around the US open.
Fear & Greed 12, the 15th day of extreme fear; November is -22.7% so far with three days left, and the worst November since 2013 was 2018's -37.0%.
Nothing new on the exit framework or the market stage; 16 straight closes below the 200-day MA.

cycle.lead: Valuation is still in the historical bottom zone while the medium-term trend evidence has tipped bearish: the weekly regime score has been negative three weeks running and one more flips it back to bear by rule; miners are under more strain than last week.
points: Weekly regime score -1.85 against -1.32 last week; it only flipped bullish on Sept 24, and the shortest of the 7 earlier bullish flips was the 8 weeks of January 2020.
Long-term holders in loss 46.0%, with this cycle's high at 46.5% on Nov 20; a close below roughly $58,000 would exceed it (CheckOnChain; the price is an estimate).

Difficulty rose 7.61% on Nov 27; the 30-day ÷ 60-day hashrate ratio fell to 0.986 and the close is only 0.5% above the estimated production cost (Bitview). Our Nov 23 second finding was refuted today.
The market stage is still bull, with 9 straight closes below a falling 200-day MA and the rule needing 30 to leave; none of the 6 supporting lights is on.

market.lead: Both walls of the range were checked today: above, short-term holders at $60,000–64,000 waiting to get out even; below, the $59,000–61,000 coins that changed hands this week. Price is squeezed tighter between them.
points: The $60,000–64,000 buckets hold 1.02M BTC of short-term holder supply; today's high of $62,139 went in for the first time and turned back (Bitview).
Over 7 days 448K BTC moved into the $59,000, $60,000 and $61,000 buckets while the $63,000 bucket lost 77K BTC (Bitview; on-chain moves are not necessarily trades).
The down leg is 67 days old and -30.9% on closes; it ends only with a close back at $67,627, 13.0% away.
The Sell Pressure Index has been maxed for 18 days with the bottom combination in place; of 20 cases since 2012, 15 exited with a gain, after a median further dip of 12% along the way.

deriv.lead: The monthly expiry has passed and downside insurance did not get cheaper; skew is more put-heavy than in yesterday's edition. Perps were quiet: today's selling pushed price down without meaningful liquidations.
points: 25-delta risk reversal -8.1 against -6.9 in yesterday's edition; 7-day implied volatility is 3.3 points above 90-day and DVOL is 51.6 (Deribit).
Option premiums have leaned to puts for 30 days; the largest Dec 4 strike is the $58,000 put with 6,571 BTC, and dealers' negative gamma is heaviest at $58,000 too (Deribit; gamma is an estimate).
Weighted funding 2.81% against 4.44% in yesterday's edition; perps saw net taker selling of 2,298 BTC and $59.1M of long liquidations for the day (Coinalyze).

The estimated long-liquidation band sits at $56.1–57.3K with 10.9K BTC (multi-exchange, an estimate); the order book shows $242M of bids at $59,000 and $224M of offers at $60,000, both on Hyperliquid perps.

flows.lead: There is no new ETF print; the Nov 27 half session shows up next edition. Every money channel we can see shows outflows slowing, and none has turned to inflow.
points: The latest complete ETF day is still Nov 25 (closed Nov 26): 7 straight outflow days totalling $2.57B (CoinMarketCap). No two sources agree on Nov 27 yet, so no provisional figure today.
Coinbase 7-day net taker selling is 2,254 BTC against 4,486 yesterday (Coinalyze); the Coinbase premium net of the USDT discount is -0.007%, about level with offshore.
Stablecoins $281.9B, down 0.53% in 7 days against 1.05% yesterday (DefiLlama); USDT at $0.9990 with a 7-day average discount of 0.143%.
Rates have not eased: the 2-year Treasury yield is 0.69 points above the Fed's upper bound, up from 0.61; Polymarket has a December hike at 96.2%.

onchain.lead: Today's finding sits on this page: back near the prior low, fewer than half as many holders were willing to sell at a loss. Sellers as a group are still in the red and the loss-taking phase is not over; the most urgent batch has sold.
points: Network realized loss was $1.28B for the day against $2.84B on Nov 20; the 7-day total is $8.14B, down from $9.70B yesterday (Bitview).
90-day realized profit ÷ loss is 0.963 against 0.982 yesterday, still falling (Bitview).
Long-term holders realized $3.49B of losses in 7 days against $4.08B yesterday; STH-SOPR is 0.985, below 1 for 22 days (CheckOnChain).

By address balance tier, addresses with 10K+ BTC added 15K BTC in 7 days and the 100–1,000 BTC tier lost 13K (Bitview); the long-term holder 30-day net position is -176K BTC, a 115th day of net reduction (bitcoin-data, Nov 26).

exit.lead: Every exit condition is far away; only the distances changed on this page today.
points: 16 straight closes below the 200-day MA at $71,811, 16.6% under it; the hedge buy-back condition was already met on Nov 17.
MVRV ÷ prior-cycle peak 0.410, with the 0.75 line at $110,417; the three top indicators read 7 / 6 / 18, all low (CoinMetrics, Nov 26).

news.title: US stocks rallied in a half session: the S&P 500 rose 1.6% to 7,297.49 and the Nasdaq 2.3% to 24,129.50; for the week the S&P 500 gained 5.6% and the Nasdaq 6.7%
news.read: Stocks rose and BTC did not follow, closing down 1.05% the same day. On this site's numbers for the last 60 US trading days, BTC gains 83.1% of the Nasdaq 100's move on up days and loses 116.9% of it on down days (through Nov 25); today is one more case. A steadier stock market removes a reason to fall without delivering buyers, and until the Nov 27 ETF flow is published there is no telling whether money came in. No change to the cycle view.

news.title: BTC fell from $62,100 to $58,700 around the Wall Street open; $228M of crypto positions were liquidated market-wide in the hour to 15:00 UTC (CoinGlass)
news.read: This site's daily bar has a high of $62,139 and a low of $58,729 (Kraken), the low only about $200 above the June 30 closing low of $58,525. Coinalyze recorded $59.1M of BTC long liquidations and $42.2M of shorts for the day, a different coverage from CoinGlass's market-wide figure, so the two are not subtracted. Both sides were hit, which says leverage sat at both ends of the range; the 1.02M BTC of short-term holder supply at $60,000–64,000 was touched for the first time today and price turned back.

news.title: The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 4.94% and the 2-year at 4.72%, up 7 basis points on the week; rate markets fully price two Fed hikes by March, with the dollar index at 104.01
news.read: On US Treasury data this site has the 2-year at 4.69%, 0.69 points above the Fed's upper bound against 0.61 yesterday; Polymarket puts a December hike at 96.2%. Stocks bounced and rates did not ease. This is macro background, not a cause we attach to BTC's moves, and it does not change the cycle view; it will not go away before the Dec 9 FOMC.

news.title: About $7B of BTC options expired on Deribit at 08:00 UTC; afterwards four of the six busiest contracts were calls, the single busiest was the Dec 25 $50,000 put, and skew still has puts pricier
news.read: Yesterday's edition said the expiry would show whether insurance gets cheaper, and today has the answer: it did not. This site's 25-delta risk reversal is -8.1 against the -6.9 in yesterday's edition, and 7-day implied volatility is 3.3 points above 90-day (Deribit). The busiest contracts are short-dated calls, small money betting on a weekend bounce; the large positions still buy downside protection, and the Dec 25 expiry now holds 48.3% of total open interest. Heavy insurance buying does not point a direction; it says the market is not treating this level as the bottom.

news.title: Bitcoin mining difficulty rose 7.61% to 145.09 T at block 977,760, almost reversing the 9.13% cut of Nov 14
news.read: Higher difficulty means the same hashrate earns fewer coins. This site's 30-day ÷ 60-day hashrate ratio fell to 0.986 and the miner-capitulation light is on for a third day; the close is only 0.5% above our difficulty-based production cost estimate (Bitview, an estimate). Blocks have slowed since the adjustment and mempool.space projects a 4.8% cut on Dec 11, a sign machines are being switched off. Miner selling is a slow variable; our Nov 23 second finding was refuted today, and the squeeze is deeper than we wrote then.

news.title: CryptoQuant: USDT supply on Ethereum and Tron fell $8.1B (4.4%) in the 60 days to Nov 23, the largest 60-day drop since August 2022; it stands at $174.5B, $12.9B below May's record
news.read: This site uses DefiLlama's total for all dollar stablecoins, down $17.5B (5.85%) in 30 days, a wider measure pointing the same way. Today's change is that the outflow slowed: down 0.53% in 7 days against 1.05% yesterday, and the 7-day average USDT discount narrowed from 0.162% to 0.143%. Stablecoins are the buying power already inside crypto, and a bounce lacks fuel while they shrink; slowing is step one, and money is back only when supply grows. No change to the cycle view.

news.title: CryptoQuant: the 7-day average of supply in profit ÷ supply in loss fell to 0.825 on Nov 26, the lowest since September 2015; the 30-day average is 1.27
news.read: This site sees the same thing: supply in profit is 46.0% (bitcoin-data, Nov 26), in the lowest 2% of the past year, and total unrealized profit is down to 33.2% of market cap, below 35% only near cycle bottoms since 2012. Readings like these describe valuation and give no guide to timing: in 2015 the stay below the floor lasted 255 days. It supports the long-term bottom-zone read and leaves the short-term view unchanged.

news.title: Tether bought 3.72M shares of miner Bitdeer on Nov 25 at about $2.69 on average, roughly $10M, lifting its stake to 17.9%; Bitdeer's stock is down 61.5% in a month and it lost $125.5M in Q3
news.read: Miner stocks have fallen further than the coin, in line with this site's miner page: the 30-day hashrate average is below the 60-day, and hashprice is $26.4 per PH per day. A cash-rich buyer picking up miner equity is what early consolidation looks like; this money went into a stock, not spot BTC. No change to any read.

news.title: Binance said on Nov 26 that its withdrawal restrictions are fully lifted, four weeks after the Oct 29 security incident; the incident involved about $6.3B, of which about $3B was frozen
news.read: The largest exchange returning to normal withdrawals removes an uncertainty that hung for four weeks. This site has USDT at $0.9990 with a 7-day average discount of 0.143%, a little narrower than yesterday's 0.162%; the narrowing and the restored withdrawals happened together, which is not the same as cause. Whether the USDT discount keeps closing toward par is what to watch. No change to any read.

actions.head: No action today.
actions.text: No new trigger: the hedge buy-back condition was met on Nov 17, and the MVRV Z 7-day average is 0.23, still below 0.5 (CoinMetrics, Nov 26).

actions.head: Don't read fewer loss-sellers as buyers coming back.
actions.text: Fewer sellers and more buyers are separate things. The ETFs had not posted a single inflow day through Nov 25, and options kept buying downside insurance after the expiry; in June this year realized losses peaked on June 6 and the price low came 24 days later, on June 30.

actions.head: The weekend is thin; Monday is the real test (Taipei time).
actions.text: The Nov 27 ETF flow should be published within two days and decides the Nov 26 finding; OPEC+ meets on Nov 29; MSCI removes Strategy from its indexes after the US close on Nov 30; payrolls land at 21:30 on Dec 4 (13:30 UTC), the same day as a Deribit weekly expiry whose largest strike is the $58,000 put.

actions.head: $58,525 below, $62,000–64,000 above.
actions.text: A close below $58,525 is a new low for this cycle; dealers' negative gamma is heaviest at $58,000 (an estimate), the estimated long-liquidation band sits at $56.1–57.3K, and below that is the realized price at $52,981 (Bitview). Above, today's high of $62,139 was sold; it takes a close above $64,000 to clear this trapped supply.

actions.head: The next levels that would move the framework are the MVRV 0.75 line at $110,417 and the $125,000 level.
actions.text: They are 84.4% and 108.8% away, both distant; the close is 16.6% below the 200-day MA at $71,811.

changes.title: Volume came back, direction did not
changes.fig: 0.38x the prior day's volume → 1.85x; daily range 2.8% → 5.6%
changes.say: Yesterday we said to watch what price does once normal volume returns, and today's answer is that both sides showed up: sellers above $62,000 and buyers at $58,700. The range stands, and the heavier volume did not pick a side.

changes.title: US spot order-book selling halved in a day
changes.say: The spot sellers stepping back, from our Nov 25 first finding, is confirmed today, and the Nov 24 first finding about a spot-led break is refuted. Fewer sell orders are hitting the book, and net buying has not appeared; ETF creations and redemptions mostly settle off-exchange and do not show in this number.

changes.title: Stablecoin outflows slowed
changes.say: Our Nov 20 second finding expired today with both conditions narrowly unmet: no break below $281B and no narrowing to within -0.5%. Money is still leaving, at half the pace.

changes.title: Downside insurance got pricier after the expiry
changes.fig: 25-delta risk reversal -6.9 → -8.1; 7-day minus 90-day implied volatility 2.9 → 3.3 points
changes.say: The monthly expiry did not take the tension with it. On-chain selling is fading while options pay more for downside cover, so the two reads disagree; the puts and negative gamma stacked at $58,000 mean volatility gets amplified if that level breaks.

changes.title: Miners are under more strain
changes.fig: 30-day ÷ 60-day hashrate 0.992 → 0.986; close above estimated production cost 1.8% → 0.5%
changes.say: Difficulty rose 7.61% on Nov 27 and price fell again, squeezing miner margins from both sides. mempool.space projects a 4.8% cut next time, and blocks have already slowed.

findings.title: Nov 20 was a capitulation low, and each retest since has drawn fewer loss-sellers
findings.lean_why: The selling side is getting lighter: back near the prior low, fewer than half as many holders were willing to sell at a loss; lows like this have been followed by gains over 30 days more often than usual, though a lower one often still comes.
findings.what: The most urgent sellers near the prior low already sold on Nov 20. Network realized losses were $2.84B that day; today price went back to $58,729 and losses were $1.28B (Bitview, Nov 27).
findings.why: First, which side moved: the sellers, while the buyers did not change. The pipeline confirmed Nov 20 as a swing low today; it sits 22% below the Sept 15 low, yet the realized-loss peak grew from 5.41 basis points of market cap to 24.03, the lower-price, bigger-loss shape of a capitulation. The two retests since were each lighter: $1.52B on Nov 25, when the low broke intraday, and $1.28B today; the 7-day total fell from $9.70B yesterday to $8.14B. Other sources point the same way: STH-SOPR bottomed at 0.9632 on Nov 20 and is 0.985 today (CheckOnChain); short-term holders realized 12.2K BTC of losses for the day, 17% less than 7 days ago; Coinbase 7-day net taker selling shrank from 4,486 BTC to 2,254 in a day (Coinalyze). The contradiction is in buyers and options: ETFs had 7 straight outflow days through Nov 25 with no new print today, and after the monthly expiry the 25-delta risk reversal is -8.1, pricier downside insurance than in yesterday's edition. Selling has ebbed and nobody has stepped in to take over.
findings.alt: The other path is that losses are smaller only because price has not broken down: on a close below $58,525 the 448K BTC that changed hands at $59,000–61,000 this week all go underwater, a new batch sells, and the loss peak may set a new high. Daily realized loss separates the two: staying below $2.84B on the next retest means selling has faded; exceeding it means Nov 20 was not the heaviest day of this leg. Data limits: Bitview counts UTXO by UTXO without entity clustering, so exchange wallet reshuffles inflate losses; the $0.54B on Nov 26 was holiday-thin and is not a trend.
findings.history: Lower-price, bigger-loss lows have mostly come late in a decline and often were not the last one. There have been about 59 such cases since 2013; of the 58 with an outcome, 44 were higher 30 days later with a median of +6.9%, against 56% and +2.8% for any day. June this year is the example: losses peaked on June 6 and the price low came 24 days later on June 30, another 3.8% lower, on smaller losses.
findings.so: What changed is one fewer reason to be bearish short-term: selling near the prior low is fading, and the larger-than-June losses in our Nov 20 first finding now look like the capitulation peak. What did not change is demand: ETFs, stablecoins and options have yet to turn, so the prior low holding only stops the fall; the market stage and the long-term bottom-zone read are unchanged too.
findings.next: By Dec 4: 7-day realized losses shrinking to within $6B confirms the ebb; any single day of realized losses above the $2.84B of Nov 20 means a larger batch has not finished selling and refutes this finding.

followups.title: ETF redemptions grew again: spot money did not follow the bid at the prior low
followups.say: No new ETF print: markets were closed on Nov 26 and the Nov 27 half session shows up next edition, so the 20-trading-day total is still -$5.35B; the close at $59,864 is 6.9% under $64,000. Deadline Dec 3.

followups.title: The break was bought back: spot sellers paused, leverage chased again
followups.say: Confirmed: Coinbase spot 7-day net taker selling narrowed to 2,254 BTC, inside 3,000, so the spot sellers did step back; the close at $59,864 stayed above $58,525. The chasing leverage has left too, with weighted funding at 2.81%.

followups.title: Sellers as a group are back in the red, 65 days after leaving
followups.say: 90-day realized profit ÷ loss is 0.963 against 0.982 yesterday, lower again and not yet at 0.95; the 30-day ratio is 0.286. Deadline Dec 3.

followups.title: $60,000 gave way to spot selling: leverage left first and there was no liquidation cascade
followups.say: Refuted: before any close below $58,525, Coinbase spot 7-day net taker selling narrowed to 2,254 BTC, inside 3,000. Spot selling faded before the prior low gave way, so the spot-led break did not carry on.

followups.title: 30-day net realized loss broke the cycle-scale line, the third time this cycle
followups.say: The 30-day net realized loss is 1.75% of market cap, short of 2%; the 7-day net loss is $7.47B, far from shrinking to $4B (CoinMetrics, Nov 26). Deadline Dec 1.

check.label: 30-day net realized loss beyond -2% of market cap

followups.title: Sold straight back at the $64K wall: loss-taking spot sold, leverage chased
followups.say: Another attempt today: the high was $62,139, sold back well short of $64,520, with the close at $59,864; long liquidations were $59.1M for the day, far from $200M. Deadline Nov 30.

followups.title: The miner-capitulation light is on by a hair: hashrate still rose 11% in a week and the squeeze is on cost
followups.say: Refuted: the 30-day ÷ 60-day hashrate ratio fell to 0.986, through 0.99, so the light is no longer on by a hair; the 30-day average is 1,000.1 EH/s and never got back to 1,015. Difficulty rose another 7.61% on Nov 27, and the squeeze on miners is deeper than we wrote then.

followups.title: Losses large enough to shrink realized cap: on-chain money down 1.5% net in a month
followups.say: The realized cap 30-day change is -1.87%, neither back within -1% nor below -2.5% (CoinMetrics, Nov 26). Deadline Nov 29, which is tomorrow.

followups.title: $55K swept leveraged longs; what bought it back is not yet spot demand
followups.say: Coinbase spot 7-day net taker selling is 2,254 BTC, halved in a day and still negative; the close at $59,864 stayed above $58,525. Sellers have backed off, and buyers turning net positive has not happened. Deadline Nov 28.

check.label: Coinbase spot 7-day net taker flow turns positive

followups.title: Price bounced, insurance got pricier: options did not treat $55K as the bottom
followups.say: The monthly expiry has passed and DVOL is 51.6, still between 50 and 60.5; the 25-delta risk reversal is -8.1, more put-heavy than the -6.9 in yesterday's edition. Deadline Nov 28.

followups.title: The prior low was tested: loss-taking is larger than at the June bottom
followups.say: Expired: in a week the close neither got back above $62,000 nor fell below $58,525, finishing at $59,864. The prior low held and the recovery did not come; today's first finding picks it up from here.

followups.title: Demand is retreating faster: stablecoin and ETF outflows widened together
followups.say: Expired: stablecoins are at $281.9B, never below $281B; the 7-day change is -0.53%, a hair short of narrowing to within -0.5%. The outflow slowed and has not stopped.

research.summary: CoinShares' Nov 27 market update expects a slow bottoming process and Galaxy on Nov 25 withdrew its call that the bear market ended in June, drawing the line at a daily close below $58,525; both fit this site's read of fading selling and absent buyers. No new issue from Glassnode, Bitfinex Alpha or K33.

items.title: Market update - November 27th, 2026: Bitcoin holds near US$61k as oversold readings meet a hawkish Fed
items.points: After core PCE came in at 3.3% y/y against 3.2% expected, BTC briefly fell below $58,000 and recovered toward $61,000; daily RSI is about 17, near the 2022 trough; MVRV is approaching the 2015, 2019 and 2022 lows without being there. Base case is a $60,000–90,000 range, with a slow bottoming process more plausible than a V-shaped recovery.
items.meaning: A slow bottom is this site's read today as well: selling is fading and buyers have not arrived. Today's close at $59,864 is already a little under its $60,000 range floor. On MVRV not being there yet we agree: 1.14, against sub-1 readings at earlier cycle bottoms (CoinMetrics, Nov 26).

items.title: BTC Looks Directionless After 7 Weeks of Losses
items.points: Withdraws its Oct 26 call that the bear market ended in June. A daily close below $58,525 or a weekly close below $59,517 confirms a new low; in the seven past cases where a standing low broke, the eventual low was at least 17.1% lower, median 51.8%. Supports listed: realized price $53,205, CVDD $48,930, long-term holder cost basis $48,357; only 2 of 13 bottom signals are met.
items.meaning: Its $58,525 line is the prior low this site has been watching, and today's intraday low of $58,729 was about $200 above it. Its supports are close to ours: realized price $52,981 and long-term holder cost $48,212 (Bitview). It counts 2 bottom signals met while most of our long-term valuation cards already lean bullish; the difference is that it waits for price to confirm.

items.title: BIT Research: When, and at What Price, Does Anthropic Become a Buy?
items.points: Mostly about equities and AI with one BTC section: the trend is bearish below $77,590, the $57,000 support flagged last week has been reached and price is recovering toward $60,000–61,000; the technical picture suggests support may not hold on a second test. It treats a Dec 9 hike as certain.
items.meaning: The second test it worries about got halfway today: the low was $58,729, short of $57,000. This site's read is that realized losses on the retest were less than half of Nov 20, so the selling side argues for a hold; the buying side offers no support, which matches its caution.

items.title: One Liners: Crypto Market Drivers — 6 Charts That Matter Now
items.points: Paywalled, preview only: BTC is trading like a high-beta stock, with a 65% correlation to the S&P 500 and 30-day volatility of 48%; miners with AI leases have held up better than those without.
items.meaning: This site has 30-day realized volatility at 47.5% (Kraken), the same, and a 30-day correlation with the Nasdaq of 0.745. Stocks rallied today and BTC closed lower, so lately that beta has only counted on the way down.

items.title: Strategy Watch #10
items.points: The institutional monthly for October: 30-day stablecoin flows turned negative on Oct 7 and exceeded $6B of outflow by month-end; US spot ETFs had a net outflow of 5,600 BTC in October, the first since July; fund managers' average cash weight rose from 12.2% to 15.7%.
items.meaning: It covers October. This site now has stablecoins down $17.5B in 30 days and ETFs at -$5.35B over 20 trading days, both far deeper than its end-October figures. No new issue: nothing dated Nov 26–28 is on the listing.

items.title: The Week On-chain: The Canary in the Coal Mine
items.points: Selling intensified after the $62–66K support broke; realized losses are the heaviest since November 2022, called the first major capitulation of this bear market; dealers are short gamma at $58–64K; below daily closes under $60K and the June low at $58.5K, the next stop is the realized price at $53.2K.
items.meaning: The major capitulation it describes is where today's first finding starts: $2.84B of realized losses on Nov 20. Today's retest reached $58,729 on $1.28B of losses, and $58.5K still holds on daily closes. No new issue.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 48
items.points: ETF weekly net outflow of $1.7B, the heaviest since early July; futures open interest down 12% to $29.3B; 25-delta skew up to 17.4%, the highest since mid-July; supply in profit 47.3% and realized cap down 0.93% on the month.
items.meaning: It says leverage was flushed, and this site sees that it has not been rebuilt: open interest is 325K BTC, down 2.8% in 7 days. Our realized cap monthly change is now -1.87%, twice as deep as its figure. The next Market Pulse is due Nov 29.

items.title: Bitcoin's Recovery Remains Elusive
items.points: Funding at 6–8% shows leveraged longs doing the buying; base case is $56,300–61,400 into the Nov 27 expiry, and a turn needs three straight ETF inflow days, $61,300 holding and STH-SOPR back at 1.
items.meaning: The expiry-day close of $59,864 landed inside its range. None of its three conditions is met: ETFs have 7 straight outflow days, the close is under $61,300 and STH-SOPR is 0.985. The leveraged longs it described have left, with weighted funding down to 2.81%. No newer issue on the listing.

items.title: No gain, plenty of pain
items.points: Paywalled, preview only: BTC broke below the 200-week MA, ETF exposure is back to mid-August and funding is negative, which it says have all lined up with BTC bottoms before.
items.meaning: The funding item on its list is now positive: weighted 2.81%. No newer issue on the listing; separately, K33 told The Block on Nov 27 that recent mathematical breakthroughs have not shown Bitcoin's cryptography to be compromised.
